chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa from Uthman ibn Isa from Usamah ibn Hafsh, who was a steward for Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him: A man marries a woman and does not specify a dowry for her, and during the conversation he said, 'I marry you upon the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet.' If he dies leaving her, or intends to consummate the marriage with her, what is her due in terms of dowry? He said: 'The dowry of the Sunnah.' I said: 'People say the dowry of her womenfolk (i.e., her female relatives).' He said: 'It is the dowry of the Sunnah.' And whenever I said something to him, he said: 'The dowry of the Sunnah.'

key_terms.فَمَا لَهَا مِنَ الْمَهْرِ: What is her due in terms of dowry; the legal entitlement of the wife regarding financial compensation.
key_terms.مَهْرُ السُّنَّةِ: The Dowry of the Sunnah; the default or standard dowry established by prophetic tradition.
key_terms.مُهُورُ نِسَائِهَا: The dowries of her womenfolk; referring to the dowries given to female relatives, used here as a contrasting concept.
key_terms.يَدْخُلَ بِهَا: To consummate the marriage; to enter into the marital union physically.

ai.seo_question: What is the default dowry (Mahr) for a woman if no specific amount is agreed upon during marriage?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) establishes 'Mahr al-Sunnah' as the default dowry when no specific amount is stipulated, countering the view that it should be determined by the bride's female relatives. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that the Sunnah provides a standardized, equitable benchmark for marital rights, ensuring financial security for the wife independent of familial social status. The repetition of the term underscores its authority as a fixed legal precedent rather than a variable custom.
